source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Has no impact on the quantity or quality of reporting, contrary to why this kind of reporting culture is actually fostered","B":"Encourages more complete, honest reporting of safety events, rather than eliminating all accountability as the new hire is currently assuming","C":"Eliminates all accountability for staff actions entirely, similar to what the new hire is currently assuming this approach actually means","D":"Applies only to reckless behavior, with no distinction from ordinary human error, which misstates how this approach actually differentiates between the two"}}
source_row.rationale: A blameless or "just culture" reporting environment, which distinguishes between simple human error, at-risk behavior, and reckless behavior (with appropriate, proportionate responses to each, per just culture principles), encourages more complete and honest reporting of safety events. This provides the organization with more accurate data to identify and address systemic issues, ultimately supporting more effective patient safety improvement than a purely punitive culture, which tends to suppress reporting.
source_row.source_detail: Impact of Reporting Culture on Safety Event Disclosure

source_row.stem: A hospital fosters a "blameless" or "just culture" reporting environment, in which staff are encouraged to report errors and near misses without fear of automatic punitive action, though a new hire assumes this just means nobody is ever held accountable for anything.
